title.narrative: Strengthening Education and Agri-business interaction for sustained employment and agricultural Development in South Africa

description.narrative:
**This project aims for the following objectives and long-term impact**
- Contribute to End hunger (SDG 2) - End poverty in all forms (SDG 1)
**Long-term impact**
- Promote agricultural growth - Create ecologically sustainable food systems - Reduce malnutrition
**Medium-term impact is defined as follows**(I) Education system (TVET/HE) is of good quality, relevant and accessible (SDG 4); (II) Partnerships between persons and organisations are inclusive and sustainable (SDG 17); (III) Organisations key to (sectoral) inclusive development of partner countries are strengthened by inflow of enhanced workforce.1) TVET/HE organisations in South Africa and the Netherlands improve core task performance, firmly embedded in their environment, and in line with national, provincial and sector specific labour market needs, whilst aiming at inclusiveness.**Output(s)**1.1 Establishment of a learning network of industry, education, NGOs and government agencies, based on a sustainable business model and effective in maximising the mutually beneficial relationships between agricultural education and the agricultural industries1.2 Mainstreaming of gender interests and interests of previously disadvantaged groups in all jointly developed approaches and products1.3 Consolidated institutional collaboration between “green” education institutes in RSA and the Netherlands1.4 Approaches based on education-industry collaboration for the best practice delivery of trade qualifications at all levels are firmly embedded in the strategies of participating organisations1.5 Sustained investments in four Education Agri-parks/networks1.6 Curricula of the participating educational institutes are jointly reviewed and adapted for inclusion of quality practical experience/internship programmes – and implemented - in cooperation with the industry, famers and other relevant stakeholders.1.7 Strengthened staff capacity of the participating educational institutes ,translating labour market demand into curriculum design, delivery and management

comment.narrative: 06-03-2023: Future food systems, Dairy production TVET, Pig production TVET, Poultry production TVET, Horticulture production TVEt and Higher Education, All on different levels.

16-03-2021: For all 4 sectors we have reviewed the curricula and formulated gaps. Next to that we had meetings with indurstry about the needs and skills requirements for graduates. Both initiatives helped to make a strategy for curricula and education program improvements. This revise of curricula is an ongoing proces. Now all networks and relations with industry are "renewed" the organisations are building a strategy to review and update the curricula yearly. | 16-03-2021: In this project we focus on 4 sectors. Dairy, Poultry and Pig production and Horticulture production. For that we have made focus on the curricula in Animal and Plant science. We have approved the practical demand and possibilities for more specialised placements.

18-07-2023: In the first project year the project focussed on 8 curricula for education. 1) Pig production 2) Poulty production 3) Dairy production 4) horticulture related curricula (under cover farming and greenhouse farming).
We found out that all important job related requirements are captured in the curricula. The roll out however was more theory focussed. For that
In the second year we focussed on short courses in leading study groups :
5) Curricula for study groups in Pig production 6) Curricula for study groups in Poultry production 7) Curricula for study groups in Beef production
Curricula for short courses 8) broilers 9) free range chickens 10) pig production 11) goat production
All this work was finalsed in the last year of the project. Working with online didactics we added this to curricula including SDGs by training lecturers on the role of future food systems in the curricula.
In the third year we developed curricula the training Future Food system 12) Introduction to systems 13 Food system in practice (case studies from industry) 14) Blended learning training (in Future food systems) 15) Applied theory in practice
Curricula for training in Farm manager (Stellenbosch University) transfer from text books to Moodle online curricula.
In addition to improving curricula we are Introduced Blended Learning in all 4 sectors. Blended Learning has two advantages: 1. Existing students can specialize more easily by combining standard education with online specialization in dairy, poultry, pig production or Horti. 2. For non students there is an open gateway to enter high quality sector education at the TVET or University of Stellenbosch
Next to the advantages it needs another teacher role, so the delivery of the curricula is reviewed and updated.

25-08-2021: In the first project year the project focused on 8 curricula for education related to Pig production, Poultry production, Dairy production and Horti culture and related curricula. comment.narrative:
16-03-2021: We foresee two actions that can support the outreach: 1. Student intervention teams. As part of the long-term relationship between SA and NL education we are planning to set up student intervention teams (students form SA and NL in mixed teams). These teams will: - Conduct a survey in the field among SME's and Emerging farmers - Based on the responses received students will develop in small teams specific knowledge products such as for instance user-friendly leaflets, apps etc. - From this survey we also identify the need for farming skills and specific skills training. This will be organised and carried out at the colleges.
2. The second action is Smartg use of Blended Learning materials. With online materials we are planning to reach out with knowledge (clips) to the society via mobile phones.

18-07-2023: 2020 1. Student intervention teams. As part of the long-term relationship between SA and NL education we are planning to set up student intervention teams (students form SA and NL in mixed teams). These teams will: - Conduct a survey in the field among SME's and Emerging farmers - Based on the responses received students will develop in small teams specific knowledge products such as for instance user-friendly leaflets, apps etc. - From this survey we also identify the need for farming skills and specific skills training. This will be organised and carried out at the colleges. 2. The second action is Smart use of Blended Learning materials. With online materials we are planning to reach out with knowledge (clips) to the society via mobile phones. In 2021 At Elangeni in this stage 152 Emerging Farmers are trained and received important skills and knowledge via the study group activity. At Stellenbosch the Future Food system training has 10 attendees. Each attendee will train with this newly gained knowledge 35 extra other people. .
